headline: NYC unveils first citywide strategy to combat antisemitism
dek: The plan doubles grants for hate-prevention groups, adds security funding for houses of worship and expands Jewish history education across New York City.
body: New York City released its first municipal Strategy to Combat Antisemitism on Tuesday, outlining a citywide plan that combines prevention, security, education, survivor support and investment in Jewish cultural institutions.

The plan includes $6.4 million in Partners Against the Hate grants for community organizations working on hate-crime prevention and survivor support, which the Mayor's Office said is twice last year's funding. It also sets aside $1 million to strengthen the physical security of synagogues and other houses of worship.

The Mayor's Office to Combat Antisemitism will help carry out a broader $26 million investment in the city's Office for the Prevention of Hate Crimes. The administration also plans to revive an interagency Security Infrastructure Working Group to provide technical and strategic assistance to Jewish houses of worship and cultural institutions.

Education and cultural projects are another part of the strategy. The city said it will expand New York City Public Schools' opportunities to visit the Museum of Jewish Heritage, invest $2 million to complete the Queens Holocaust memorial and provide $2.5 million for the Center for New Jewish Culture in Central Brooklyn.

The strategy calls for seven lines of work, including preventing hate violence, addressing physical, verbal and digital antisemitism, supporting survivors, protecting Jewish life and listening to Jewish communities. A planned City Human Rights Law campaign on LinkNYC kiosks and in other public spaces will explain how residents can report suspected discrimination.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: NYC Unveils Strategy to Combat Antisemitism
seoDescription: New York City released its first municipal strategy to combat antisemitism, with new funding for hate prevention, worship-site security, education and cultural institutions.
